stories.title: 📜 Isaia 1
summaryBullets: Visione che Isaia, figlio di Amots, ebbe riguardo a Giuda e a Gerusalemme ai giorni di Uzzia, di Iotam, di Acaz e di Ezechia, re di Giuda. (1:1).
"Hear, O heavens, and give ear, O earth; for il SIGNORE has spoken: 'Children I have reared and brought up, but they have rebelled against Me'" (1:2).
The ox knows its owner, and the donkey its master's manger, but Israel does not know; My people do not understand (1:3).
Ah, sinful nation, a people laden with iniquity, offspring of evildoers, children who deal corruptly! They have forsaken il SIGNORE and despised the Holy One of Israel (1:4).
Why will you still be struck down? The whole head is sick and the whole heart faint (1:5).
Dalla pianta del piede fino alla testa non c’è nulla di sano in esso: non ci sono che ferite, contusioni, piaghe aperte, che non sono state ripulite, né fasciate, né lenite con olio. (1:6).
Your country lies desolate; your cities are burned with fire; in your very presence foreigners devour your land (1:7).
The daughter of Zion is left like a booth in a vineyard, like a lodge in a cucumber field, like a besieged city (1:8).
If il SIGNORE of hosts had not left us a few survivors, we would have been like Sodom and become like Gomorrah (1:9).
Ascoltate la parola del Signore, capi di Sodoma! Prestate orecchio alla legge del nostro Dio, popolo di Gomorra! (1:10).

«Che m’importa dei vostri numerosi sacrifici?», dice il Signore; «io sono sazio degli olocausti di montoni e del grasso di bestie ingrassate; il sangue dei tori, degli agnelli e dei capri, io non lo gradisco. (1:11).
"When you come to appear before Me, who has required of you this trampling of My courts?" (1:12).
"Bring no more vain offerings; incense is an abomination to Me. New moon and Sabbath and the calling of convocations—I cannot endure iniquity and solemn assembly" (1:13).
"Your new moons and your appointed feasts My soul hates; they have become a burden to Me; I am weary of bearing them" (1:14).
"When you spread out your hands, I will hide My eyes from you; even though you make many prayers, I will not listen; your hands are full of blood" (1:15).
"Wash yourselves; make yourselves clean; remove the evil of your deeds from before My eyes; cease to do evil" (1:16).
"Learn to do good; seek justice; correct oppression; bring justice to the fatherless; plead the widow's cause" (1:17).
"Come now, let us reason together," says il SIGNORE. "Though your sins are like scarlet, they shall be as white as snow; though they are red like crimson, they shall become like wool" (1:18).
Se siete disposti a ubbidire, mangerete i frutti migliori del paese; (1:19).
ma se rifiutate e siete ribelli, sarete divorati dalla spada», poiché la bocca del Signore ha parlato. (1:20).
How the faithful city has become a whore! She who was full of justice—righteousness lodged in her, but now murderers (1:21).
Your silver has become dross; your wine is mixed with water (1:22).
I tuoi prìncipi sono ribelli e compagni di ladri. Tutti amano i regali e corrono dietro alle ricompense; non fanno giustizia all’orfano e la causa della vedova non giunge fino a loro. (1:23).
Therefore the Lord declares, il SIGNORE of hosts, the Mighty One of Israel: "Ah, I will get relief from My enemies and avenge Myself on My foes" (1:24).
"I will turn My hand against you and will smelt away your dross as with lye and remove all your alloy" (1:25).
"And I will restore your judges as at the first and your counselors as at the beginning. Afterward you shall be called the city of righteousness, the faithful city" (1:26).
Zion shall be redeemed by justice, and those in her who repent, by righteousness (1:27).
ma i ribelli e i peccatori andranno in rovina assieme, e quelli che abbandonano il Signore saranno distrutti. (1:28).
Allora avrete vergogna dei terebinti che avete amati e arrossirete dei giardini che vi siete scelti. (1:29).
For you shall be like an oak whose leaf withers, and like a garden without water (1:30).
And the strong shall become tinder, and his work a spark, and both of them shall burn together, with none to quench them (1:31).

stories.title: 🏔️ Isaia 2
summaryBullets: Parola che Isaia, figlio di Amots, ebbe in visione riguardo a Giuda e a Gerusalemme. (2:1).
Avverrà, negli ultimi giorni, che il monte della casa del Signore si ergerà sulla vetta dei monti e sarà elevato al di sopra dei colli; e tutte le nazioni affluiranno a esso. (2:2).

Molti popoli vi accorreranno e diranno: «Venite, saliamo al monte del Signore, alla casa del Dio di Giacobbe; egli ci insegnerà le sue vie e noi cammineremo per i suoi sentieri». Da Sion, infatti, uscirà la legge, e da Gerusalemme la parola del Signore. (2:3).

He shall judge between the nations and shall decide disputes for many peoples; they shall beat their swords into plowshares and their spears into pruning hooks; nation shall not lift up sword against nation, neither shall they learn war anymore (2:4).
O house of Jacob, come, let us walk in the light of il SIGNORE (2:5).

Infatti tu, Signore, hai abbandonato il tuo popolo, la casa di Giacobbe, perché sono pieni di pratiche divinatorie, praticano le arti occulte come i Filistei, fanno alleanza con i figli degli stranieri. (2:6).
Their land is filled with silver and gold, and there is no end to their treasures; their land is filled with horses, and there is no end to their chariots (2:7).
Their land is filled with idols; they bow down to the work of their hands, to what their own fingers have made (2:8).
So man is humbled, and each one is brought low—do not forgive them! (2:9).
Entra nella roccia e nasconditi nella polvere per sottrarti al terrore del Signore e allo splendore della sua maestà. (2:10).
Lo sguardo altero dell’uomo sarà umiliato e l’orgoglio di ognuno sarà abbassato; il Signore solo sarà esaltato in quel giorno. (2:11).
For il SIGNORE of hosts has a day against all that is proud and lofty, against all that is lifted up—and it shall be brought low (2:12).
Against all the cedars of Lebanon, lofty and lifted up, and against all the oaks of Bashan (2:13).
Against all the lofty mountains and against all the uplifted hills (2:14).
Against every high tower and against every fortified wall (2:15).
Against all the ships of Tarshish and against all the beautiful craft (2:16).
L’alterigia dell’uomo sarà umiliata, e l’orgoglio di ognuno sarà abbassato; il Signore solo sarà esaltato in quel giorno. (2:17).
And the idols shall utterly pass away (2:18).
Gli uomini entreranno nelle caverne delle rocce e negli antri della terra per sottrarsi al terrore del Signore e allo splendore della sua maestà, quando egli sorgerà per far tremare la terra. (2:19).
In quel giorno gli uomini getteranno ai topi e ai pipistrelli gli idoli d’argento e d’oro che si erano fatti per adorarli; (2:20).
ed entreranno nelle fessure delle rocce e nei crepacci delle rupi per sottrarsi al terrore del Signore e allo splendore della sua maestà, quando egli sorgerà per far tremare la terra. (2:21).
Stop regarding man in whose nostrils is breath, for of what account is he? (2:22).

stories.title: 🏔️ Isaia 3
summaryBullets: For behold, the Lord GOD of hosts is taking away from Jerusalem and from Judah support and supply, all support of bread and all support of water (3:1).
il prode e il guerriero, il giudice e il profeta, l’indovino e l’anziano, (3:2).
il capo di cinquantina e il notabile, il consigliere, l’artefice esperto e l’abile incantatore. (3:3).
And I will make boys their princes, and infants shall rule over them (3:4).
Il popolo sarà oppresso, uomo da uomo, ciascuno dal suo prossimo; il giovane sarà arrogante con il vecchio, l’infame contro colui che è onorato. (3:5).
Quando uno prenderà il fratello nella sua casa paterna e gli dirà: «Tu hai un mantello, sii nostro capo, prendi in mano queste rovine», (3:6).
egli, in quel giorno, alzerà la voce e dirà: «Io non sarò vostro medico, nella mia casa non c’è né pane né mantello; non fatemi capo del popolo!» (3:7).
For Jerusalem has stumbled and Judah has fallen, because their speech and their deeds are against il SIGNORE, defying His glorious presence (3:8).
For the look on their faces bears witness against them; they proclaim their sin like Sodom; they do not hide it. Woe to them, for they have brought evil on themselves (3:9).
Tell the righteous that it shall be well with them, for they shall eat the fruit of their deeds (3:10).
Guai all’empio! Il male ricadrà sul suo capo, perché gli sarà reso quanto le sue mani hanno fatto. (3:11).
My people—infants are their oppressors, and women rule over them. O My people, your guides mislead you and they have swallowed up the course of your paths (3:12).
The LORD has taken His place to contend; He stands to judge peoples (3:13).
Il Signore entra in giudizio con gli anziani del suo popolo e con i prìncipi di esso: «Voi siete quelli che hanno devastato la vigna! Le spoglie del povero sono nelle vostre case! (3:14).
Con quale diritto opprimete il mio popolo e pestate la faccia agli indifesi?», dice il Signore, Dio degli eserciti. (3:15).
The LORD said: Because the daughters of Zion are haughty and walk with outstretched necks, glancing wantonly with their eyes, mincing along as they go, tinkling with their feet (3:16).
il Signore farà venire la tigna sulla testa delle figlie di Sion, il Signore metterà a nudo le loro vergogne. (3:17).
In quel giorno il Signore toglierà via il lusso degli anelli dei piedi, delle reti e delle mezzelune, (3:18).
The pendants, the bracelets, and the scarves (3:19).
The headdresses, the armlets, the sashes, the perfume boxes, and the amulets (3:20).
The signet rings and nose rings (3:21).
The festal robes, the mantles, the cloaks, and the handbags (3:22).
The mirrors, the linen garments, the turbans, and the veils (3:23).
Instead of perfume there will be rottenness; instead of a belt, a rope; instead of well-set hair, baldness; instead of a rich robe, a skirt of sackcloth; and branding instead of beauty (3:24).
Your men shall fall by the sword and your mighty men in battle (3:25).
And her gates shall lament and mourn; empty, she shall sit on the ground (3:26).

stories.title: 🏔️ Isaia 4
summaryBullets: And seven women shall take hold of one man in that day, saying, "We will eat our own bread and wear our own clothes, only let us be called by your name; take away our reproach" (4:1).
In quel giorno il germoglio del Signore sarà lo splendore e la gloria degli scampati d’Israele, e il frutto della terra sarà il loro vanto e il loro ornamento. (4:2).
And he who is left in Zion and remains in Jerusalem will be called holy, everyone who has been recorded for life in Jerusalem (4:3).

una volta che il Signore avrà lavato le brutture delle figlie di Sion, e avrà purificato Gerusalemme dal sangue che vi è stato sparso, con il soffio del giudizio e con il soffio dello sterminio. (4:4).

Then il SIGNORE will create over the whole site of Mount Zion and over her assemblies a cloud by day, and smoke and the shining of a flaming fire by night; for over all the glory there will be a canopy (4:5).
Ci sarà un riparo per fare ombra di giorno e proteggere dal caldo, e per servire di rifugio e di asilo durante la tempesta e la pioggia. (4:6).

stories.title: 🍇 Isaia 5
summaryBullets: Let me sing for my beloved my love song concerning his vineyard: My beloved had a vineyard on a very fertile hill (5:1).

He dug it and cleared it of stones and planted it with choice vines; he built a watchtower in the midst of it and hewed out a wine vat in it; and he looked for it to yield grapes, but it yielded wild grapes (5:2).
"And now, O inhabitants of Jerusalem and men of Judah, judge between me and my vineyard" (5:3).
"What more was there to do for my vineyard that I have not done in it? When I looked for it to yield grapes, why did it yield wild grapes?" (5:4).
Ebbene, ora vi farò conoscere ciò che sto per fare alla mia vigna: le toglierò la siepe e vi pascoleranno le bestie; abbatterò il suo muro di cinta e sarà calpestata. (5:5).
"I will make it a waste; it shall not be pruned or hoed, and briers and thorns shall grow up; I will also command the clouds that they rain no rain upon it" (5:6).

Infatti la vigna del Signore degli eserciti è la casa d’Israele, e gli uomini di Giuda sono la sua piantagione prediletta. Egli si aspettava rettitudine, ed ecco spargimento di sangue; giustizia, ed ecco grida d’angoscia! (5:7).
Guai a quelli che aggiungono casa a casa, che uniscono campo a campo, finché non rimanga più spazio, e voi restiate soli ad abitare nel paese! (5:8).
Questo mi ha detto all’orecchio il Signore degli eserciti: «In verità case numerose saranno desolate, queste case grandi e belle saranno private d’abitanti; (5:9).
For ten acres of vineyard shall yield but one bath, and a homer of seed shall yield but an ephah (5:10).
Woe to those who rise early in the morning, that they may run after strong drink, who tarry late into the evening as wine inflames them (5:11).
They have lyre and harp, tambourine and flute and wine at their feasts, but they do not regard the deeds of il SIGNORE or see the work of His hands (5:12).
Therefore my people go into exile for lack of knowledge; their honored men go hungry, and their multitude is parched with thirst (5:13).
Therefore Sheol has enlarged its appetite and opened its mouth beyond measure, and the nobility of Jerusalem and her multitude will go down, her revelers and he who exults in her (5:14).
L’uomo è umiliato, ognuno è abbassato, e abbassati sono gli sguardi alteri; (5:15).
But il SIGNORE of hosts is exalted in justice, and the Holy God shows Himself holy in righteousness (5:16).
Then shall the lambs graze as in their pasture, and nomads shall eat among the ruins of the rich (5:17).
Woe to those who draw iniquity with cords of falsehood, who draw sin as with cart ropes (5:18).
Who say, "Let Him be quick, let Him speed His work that we may see it; let the counsel of the Holy One of Israel draw near and let it come, that we may know it!" (5:19).
Woe to those who call evil good and good evil, who put darkness for light and light for darkness, who put bitter for sweet and sweet for bitter (5:20).
Woe to those who are wise in their own eyes and shrewd in their own sight (5:21).
Woe to those who are heroes at drinking wine and valiant men in mixing strong drink (5:22).
Who acquit the guilty for a bribe and deprive the innocent of his right (5:23).

Perciò, come una lingua di fuoco divora la stoppia e come la fiamma consuma l’erba secca, così la loro radice sarà come marciume, e il loro fiore sarà portato via come polvere; perché hanno rifiutato la legge del Signore degli eserciti e hanno disprezzato la parola del Santo d’Israele. (5:24).

Per questo divampa l’ira del Signore contro il suo popolo; egli stende contro di esso la sua mano e lo colpisce; tremano i monti, i cadaveri sono come spazzatura in mezzo alle vie; con tutto ciò, la sua ira non si calma e la sua mano rimane distesa. (5:25).
Egli alza un vessillo per le nazioni lontane; fischia a un popolo, che è all’estremità della terra; ed eccolo che arriva, pronto, leggero. (5:26).
None is weary, none stumbles, none slumbers or sleeps, not a waistband is loose, not a sandal strap broken (5:27).
Their arrows are sharp, all their bows bent, their horses' hoofs seem like flint, and their wheels like the whirlwind (5:28).
Their roaring is like a lion, like young lions they roar; they growl and seize their prey; they carry it off, and none can rescue (5:29).
In quel giorno egli muggirà contro Giuda come mugge il mare; e, a guardare il paese, ecco tenebre, angoscia e la luce che si oscura mediante le sue nuvole. (5:30).

stories.title: 🔥 Isaia 6
summaryBullets: Nell’anno della morte del re Uzzia vidi il Signore seduto sopra un trono alto, molto elevato, e i lembi del suo mantello riempivano il tempio. (6:1).
Above Him stood the seraphim. Each had six wings: with two he covered his face, and with two he covered his feet, and with two he flew (6:2).
And one called to another and said, "Holy, holy, holy is il SIGNORE of hosts; the whole earth is full of His glory!" (6:3).
Le porte furono scosse fin dalle loro fondamenta dalla voce di loro che gridavano, e la casa fu piena di fumo. (6:4).

Allora io dissi: «Guai a me, sono perduto! Perché io sono un uomo dalle labbra impure e abito in mezzo a un popolo dalle labbra impure; e i miei occhi hanno visto il Re, il Signore degli eserciti!» (6:5).
Ma uno dei serafini volò verso di me, tenendo in mano un carbone ardente, tolto con le molle dall’altare. (6:6).
And he touched his mouth and said, "Behold, this has touched your lips; your guilt is taken away, and your sin atoned for" (6:7).
And Isaiah heard the voice of the Lord saying, "Whom shall I send, and who will go for Us?" Then he said, "Here I am! Send me" (6:8).
And He said, "Go, and say to this people: 'Keep on hearing, but do not understand; keep on seeing, but do not perceive'" (6:9).

"Make the heart of this people dull, and their ears heavy, and blind their eyes; lest they see with their eyes and hear with their ears and understand with their hearts and turn and be healed" (6:10).
Then Isaiah said, "How long, O Lord?" And He said, "Until cities lie waste without inhabitant, and houses without people, and the land is a desolate waste" (6:11).
finché il Signore abbia allontanato gli uomini, e la solitudine sia grande in mezzo al paese. (6:12).
"And though a tenth remain in it, it will be burned again, like a terebinth or an oak, whose stump remains when it is felled. The holy seed is its stump" (6:13).

stories.title: 👶 Isaia 7
summaryBullets: Ai giorni di Acaz, figlio di Iotam, figlio di Uzzia, re di Giuda, Resin, re di Siria, e Peca, figlio di Remalia, re d’Israele, salirono contro Gerusalemme per muoverle guerra; ma non riuscirono a espugnarla. (7:1).

Fu riferita alla casa di Davide questa notizia: «La Siria si è confederata con Efraim». Il cuore di Acaz e il cuore del suo popolo furono agitati, come gli alberi della foresta sono agitati dal vento. (7:2).
Allora il Signore disse a Isaia: «Va’ incontro ad Acaz, tu con Sear-Iasub, tuo figlio, verso l’estremità dell’acquedotto della vasca superiore, sulla strada del campo del lavandaio e digli: (7:3).

"And say to him, 'Be careful, be quiet, do not fear, and do not let your heart be faint because of these two smoldering stumps of firebrands, at the fierce anger of Rezin and Syria and figlio di Remaliah'" (7:4).
"Because Syria, with Ephraim and figlio di Remaliah, has devised evil against you, saying" (7:5).
"'Let us go up against Judah and terrify it, and let us conquer it for ourselves, and set up figlio di Tabeel as king in the midst of it'" (7:6).
Thus says the Lord GOD: "It shall not stand, and it shall not come to pass" (7:7).
Poiché Damasco è la capitale della Siria e Resin è il capo di Damasco, in sessantacinque anni Efraim sarà fiaccato al punto che non sarà più popolo. (7:8).
Samaria è la capitale di Efraim e il figlio di Remalia è il capo di Samaria. Se voi non avete fede, certo, non potrete sussistere”. (7:9).
Again il SIGNORE spoke to Ahaz (7:10).
"Ask a sign of il SIGNORE your God; let it be deep as Sheol or high as heaven" (7:11).
But Ahaz said, "I will not ask, and I will not put il SIGNORE to the test" (7:12).
And Isaiah said, "Hear then, O house of David! Is it too little for you to weary men, that you weary my God also?" (7:13).
"Therefore the Lord Himself will give you a sign. Behold, the virgin shall conceive and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel" (7:14).
He shall eat curds and honey when he knows how to refuse the evil and choose the good (7:15).
For before the boy knows how to refuse the evil and choose the good, the land whose two kings you dread will be deserted (7:16).
«Il Signore farà venire su di te, sul tuo popolo e sulla casa di tuo padre dei giorni come non se ne ebbero mai dal giorno che Efraim si è separato da Giuda, vale a dire il re d’Assiria. (7:17).
In quel giorno il Signore fischierà alle mosche che sono all’estremità dei fiumi d’Egitto e alle api che sono nel paese d’Assiria. (7:18).
Esse verranno e si poseranno tutte nelle valli deserte, nelle fessure delle rocce, su tutti i cespugli e su tutti i pascoli. (7:19).
In quel giorno il Signore, con un rasoio preso a noleggio di là dal fiume, cioè con il re d’Assiria, raderà la testa, i peli dei piedi e porterà via anche la barba. (7:20).
In that day a man will keep alive a young cow and two sheep (7:21).
ed esse daranno tale abbondanza di latte, che egli mangerà panna; poiché panna e miele mangerà chiunque sarà rimasto superstite nel paese. (7:22).
In that day every place where there used to be a thousand vines, worth a thousand shekels of silver, will become briers and thorns (7:23).
With bow and arrows a man will come there, for all the land will be briers and thorns (7:24).
And as for all the hills that used to be hoed with a hoe, you will not go there for fear of briers and thorns, but they will become a place where cattle are let loose and where sheep tread (7:25).

stories.title: 👶 Isaia 8
summaryBullets: Then il SIGNORE said to Isaiah, "Take a large tablet and write on it in common characters, 'Belonging to Maher-shalal-hash-baz'" (8:1).
And Isaiah got reliable witnesses, Uriah il sacerdote and Zechariah figlio di Jeberechiah, to attest for him (8:2).
Mi unii pure alla profetessa, e lei concepì e partorì un figlio. Allora il Signore mi disse: «Chiamalo “Affrettate il saccheggio. Presto al bottino”; (8:3).
poiché prima che il bambino sappia chiamare papà e mamma, le ricchezze di Damasco e il bottino di Samaria saranno portati davanti al re d’Assiria». (8:4).
The LORD spoke to Isaiah again (8:5).
"Because this people has refused the waters of Shiloah that flow gently, and rejoice over Rezin and figlio di Remaliah" (8:6).

ecco, il Signore sta per far salire su di loro le potenti e grandi acque del fiume, cioè il re d’Assiria e tutta la sua gloria; esso s’innalzerà dappertutto sopra il suo livello, e strariperà su tutte le sue sponde. (8:7).
"And it will sweep on into Judah, it will overflow and pass on, reaching even to the neck, and its outspread wings will fill the breadth of your land, O Immanuel" (8:8).
"Be broken, you peoples, and be shattered; give ear, all you far countries; strap on your armor and be shattered; strap on your armor and be shattered" (8:9).
"Take counsel together, but it will come to nothing; speak a word, but it will not stand, for God is with us" (8:10).
For il SIGNORE spoke thus to me with His strong hand upon me and warned me not to walk in the way of this people, saying (8:11).
"Do not call conspiracy all that this people calls conspiracy, and do not fear what they fear, nor be in dread" (8:12).
"But il SIGNORE of hosts, Him you shall honor as holy. Let Him be your fear, and let Him be your dread" (8:13).
"And He will become a sanctuary and a stone of offense and a rock of stumbling to both houses of Israel, a trap and a snare to the inhabitants of Jerusalem" (8:14).
And many shall stumble on it. They shall fall and be broken; they shall be snared and taken (8:15).
Bind up the testimony; seal the teaching among my disciples (8:16).
I will wait for il SIGNORE, who is hiding His face from the house of Jacob, and I will hope in Him (8:17).
Behold, I and the children whom il SIGNORE has given me are signs and portents in Israel from il SIGNORE of hosts, who dwells on Mount Zion (8:18).

Se vi si dice: «Consultate quelli che evocano gli spiriti e gli indovini, quelli che sussurrano e bisbigliano», rispondete: «Un popolo non deve forse consultare il suo Dio? Si rivolgerà forse ai morti in favore dei vivi? (8:19).
Alla legge! Alla testimonianza!» Se il popolo non parla così, non vi sarà per lui nessuna aurora! (8:20).

They will pass through the land, greatly distressed and hungry. And when they are hungry, they will be enraged and will speak contemptuously against their king and their God, and turn their faces upward (8:21).
And they will look to the earth, but behold, distress and darkness, the gloom of anguish. And they will be thrust into thick darkness (8:22).

stories.title: 🌅 Isaia 9
summaryBullets: Il popolo che camminava nelle tenebre vede una gran luce; su quelli che abitavano il paese dell’ombra della morte la luce risplende. (9:1).
The people who walked in darkness have seen a great light; those who dwelt in a land of deep darkness, on them has light shone (9:2).
You have multiplied the nation; You have increased its joy; they rejoice before You as with joy at the harvest, as they are glad when they divide the spoil (9:3).
Difatti ogni calzatura portata dal guerriero nella mischia, ogni mantello sporco di sangue saranno dati alle fiamme, saranno divorati dal fuoco. (9:4).
Poiché un bambino ci è nato, un figlio ci è stato dato, e il dominio riposerà sulle sue spalle; sarà chiamato Consigliere ammirabile, Dio potente, Padre eterno, Principe della pace, (9:5).

per dare incremento all’impero e una pace senza fine al trono di Davide e al suo regno, per stabilirlo fermamente e sostenerlo mediante il diritto e la giustizia, da ora e per sempre: questo farà lo zelo del Signore degli eserciti. (9:6).

Of the increase of his government and of peace there will be no end, on the throne of David and over his kingdom, to establish it and to uphold it with justice and with righteousness from this time forth and forevermore. The zeal of il SIGNORE of hosts will do this (9:7).
The Lord has sent a word against Jacob, and it will fall on Israel (9:8).
«I mattoni sono caduti, ma noi costruiremo con pietre squadrate; i sicomori sono stati tagliati, ma noi li sostituiremo con cedri». (9:9).
"The bricks have fallen, but we will build with dressed stones; the sycamores have been cut down, but we will put cedars in their place" (9:10).
But il SIGNORE raises the adversaries of Rezin against them and stirs up their enemies (9:11).
The Syrians on the east and the Philistines on the west devour Israel with open mouth. For all this His anger has not turned away, and His hand is stretched out still (9:12).
The people did not turn to Him who struck them, nor inquire of il SIGNORE of hosts (9:13).
So il SIGNORE cut off from Israel head and tail, palm branch and reed in one day (9:14).
The elder and honored man is the head, and the prophet who teaches lies is the tail (9:15).
For those who guide this people have been leading them astray, and those who are guided by them are swallowed up (9:16).

Therefore the Lord does not rejoice over their young men, and has no compassion on their fatherless and widows; for everyone is godless and an evildoer, and every mouth speaks folly. For all this His anger has not turned away, and His hand is stretched out still (9:17).
For wickedness burns like a fire; it consumes briers and thorns; it kindles the thickets of the forest, and they roll upward in a column of smoke (9:18).
Si saccheggia a destra e si ha fame; si divora a sinistra e non si è saziati; ognuno divora la carne del proprio braccio: (9:19).
They slice meat on the right but are still hungry, and they devour on the left but are not satisfied; each devours the flesh of his own arm (9:20).
Manasseh devours Ephraim, and Ephraim devours Manasseh; together they are against Judah. For all this His anger has not turned away, and His hand is stretched out still (9:21).

stories.title: ⚔️ Isaia 10
summaryBullets: Woe to those who decree iniquitous decrees, and the writers who keep writing oppression (10:1).
To turn aside the needy from justice and to rob the poor of My people of their right, that widows may be their spoil and that they may make the fatherless their prey (10:2).
What will you do on the day of punishment, in the ruin that will come from afar? To whom will you flee for help, and where will you leave your wealth? (10:3).
Nothing remains but to crouch among the prisoners or fall among the slain. For all this His anger has not turned away, and His hand is stretched out still (10:4).
"Woe to Assyria, the rod of My anger; the staff in their hands is My fury!" (10:5).
Io la mando contro una nazione empia e la dirigo contro il popolo che ha provocato la mia ira, con l’ordine di darsi al saccheggio, di far bottino, di calpestarlo come il fango delle strade. (10:6).
But he does not so intend, and his heart does not so think; but it is in his heart to destroy and to cut off nations not a few (10:7).
For he says, "Are not my commanders all kings?" (10:8).
"Is not Calno like Carchemish? Is not Hamath like Arpad? Is not Samaria like Damascus?" (10:9).
Come la mia mano è giunta a colpire i regni degli idoli dove le immagini erano più numerose che a Gerusalemme e a Samaria, (10:10).
"Shall I not do to Jerusalem and her idols as I have done to Samaria and her images?" (10:11).

Ma quando il Signore avrà compiuto tutta la sua opera sul monte Sion e a Gerusalemme, «io», dice il Signore, «punirò il re d’Assiria per il frutto della superbia del suo cuore e dell’arroganza dei suoi sguardi alteri. (10:12).

For he says, "By the strength of my hand I have done it, and by my wisdom, for I have understanding; I remove the boundaries of peoples and have plundered their treasures; like a bull I bring down those who sit on thrones" (10:13).

La mia mano ha trovato, come un nido, le ricchezze dei popoli; e come uno raccoglie delle uova abbandonate, così io ho raccolto tutta la terra, e nessuno ha mosso l’ala o aperto il becco o mandato un grido”». (10:14).

Shall the axe boast over him who hews with it, or the saw magnify itself against him who wields it? As if a rod should wield him who lifts it, or as if a staff should lift him who is not wood! (10:15).
Therefore the Lord GOD of hosts will send wasting sickness among his stout warriors, and under his glory a burning will be kindled, like the burning of fire (10:16).
The light of Israel will become a fire, and his Holy One a flame, and it will burn and devour his thorns and briers in one day (10:17).
The glory of his forest and of his fruitful land il SIGNORE will destroy, both soul and body, and it will be as when a sick man wastes away (10:18).
The remnant of the trees of his forest will be so few that a child can write them down (10:19).

In quel giorno il residuo d’Israele e gli scampati della casa di Giacobbe smetteranno di appoggiarsi su colui che li colpiva, e si appoggeranno con sincerità sul Signore, sul Santo d’Israele. (10:20).
A remnant will return, the remnant of Jacob, to the mighty God (10:21).
For though your people Israel be as the sand of the sea, only a remnant of them will return. Destruction is decreed, overflowing with righteousness (10:22).
Poiché lo sterminio che ha decretato, il Signore, Dio degli eserciti, lo effettuerà in mezzo a tutto il paese. (10:23).
Così dunque dice il Signore, Dio degli eserciti: «Popolo mio, che abiti a Sion, non temere l’Assiro che ti batte con la verga e alza su di te il bastone, come fece l’Egitto! (10:24).
"For in a very little while My fury will come to an end, and My anger will be directed to their destruction" (10:25).
And il SIGNORE of hosts will wield against them a whip, as when He struck Midian at the rock of Oreb. And His staff will be over the sea, and He will lift it as He did in Egypt (10:26).
In quel giorno il suo carico ti cadrà dalle spalle e il suo giogo dal collo; il giogo sarà scosso dalla tua forza rigogliosa. (10:27).
L’Assiro marcia contro Aiat, attraversa Migron, depone i suoi bagagli a Micmas. (10:28).
They have crossed over the pass; at Geba they lodge for the night; Ramah trembles; Gibeah of Saul has fled (10:29).
Cry aloud, O daughter of Gallim! Give attention, O Laishah! O poor Anathoth! (10:30).
Madmenah is in flight; the inhabitants of Gebim flee for safety (10:31).

stories.title: ⚔️ Isaia 11
summaryBullets: There shall come forth a shoot from the stump of Jesse, and a branch from his roots shall bear fruit (11:1).
Lo Spirito del Signore riposerà su di lui: Spirito di saggezza e d’intelligenza, Spirito di consiglio e di forza, Spirito di conoscenza e di timore del Signore. (11:2).
Respirerà come profumo il timore del Signore, non giudicherà dall’apparenza, non darà sentenze stando al sentito dire, (11:3).
ma giudicherà i poveri con giustizia, pronuncerà sentenze eque per gli umili del paese. Colpirà il paese con la verga della sua bocca, e con il soffio delle sue labbra farà morire l’empio. (11:4).
Righteousness shall be the belt of his waist, and faithfulness the belt of his loins (11:5).
Il lupo abiterà con l’agnello, e il leopardo si sdraierà accanto al capretto; il vitello, il leoncello e il bestiame ingrassato staranno assieme, e un bambino li condurrà. (11:6).
La vacca pascolerà con l’orsa, i loro piccoli si sdraieranno assieme e il leone mangerà il foraggio come il bue. (11:7).
Il lattante giocherà sul nido della vipera, e il bambino divezzato stenderà la mano nella buca del serpente. (11:8).
Non si farà né male né danno su tutto il mio monte santo, poiché la conoscenza del Signore riempirà la terra, come le acque coprono il fondo del mare. (11:9).
In quel giorno verso la radice d’Isai, issata come vessillo dei popoli, si volgeranno premurose le nazioni, e la sua residenza sarà gloriosa. (11:10).

In quel giorno il Signore stenderà una seconda volta la mano per riscattare il residuo del suo popolo rimasto in Assiria e in Egitto, a Patros e in Etiopia, a Elam, a Scinear e a Camat, e nelle isole del mare. (11:11).
Egli alzerà un vessillo verso le nazioni, raccoglierà gli esuli d’Israele e radunerà i dispersi di Giuda dai quattro canti della terra. (11:12).
The jealousy of Ephraim shall depart, and those who harass Judah shall be cut off; Ephraim shall not be jealous of Judah, and Judah shall not harass Ephraim (11:13).

Essi piomberanno a volo sulle spalle dei Filistei a occidente, insieme faranno razzia tra i figli dell’oriente; metteranno le mani addosso a Edom e a Moab, e i figli di Ammon saranno loro sudditi. (11:14).

And il SIGNORE will utterly destroy the tongue of the Sea of Egypt, and will wave His hand over the River with His scorching breath, and strike it into seven channels, and He will lead people across in sandals (11:15).
Ci sarà una strada per il residuo del suo popolo rimasto in Assiria, come ce ne fu una per Israele il giorno che uscì dal paese d’Egitto. (11:16).

summaryBullets: You will say in that day: "I will give thanks to You, O LORD, for though You were angry with me, Your anger turned away, that You might comfort me" (12:1).
"Behold, God is my salvation; I will trust, and will not be afraid; for il SIGNORE GOD is my strength and my song, and He has become my salvation" (12:2).
With joy you will draw water from the wells of salvation (12:3).
And you will say in that day: "Give thanks to il SIGNORE, call upon His name, make known His deeds among the peoples, proclaim that His name is exalted" (12:4).
"Sing praises to il SIGNORE, for He has done gloriously; let this be made known in all the earth" (12:5).
"Shout, and sing for joy, O inhabitant of Zion, for great in your midst is the Holy One of Israel" (12:6).

stories.title: 🏛️ Isaia 13
summaryBullets: The oracle concerning Babylon which Isaiah figlio di Amoz saw (13:1).
On a bare hill raise a signal; cry aloud to them; wave the hand for them to enter the gates of the nobles (13:2).
"I Myself have commanded My consecrated ones, and have summoned My mighty men to execute My anger, My proudly exulting ones" (13:3).
The sound of a tumult is on the mountains, like a great multitude! The sound of an uproar of kingdoms, of nations gathering together! The LORD of hosts is mustering a host for battle (13:4).
Vengono da un paese lontano, dall’estremità dei cieli, il Signore e gli strumenti della sua ira, per distruggere tutto il paese. (13:5).
Urlate, poiché il giorno del Signore è vicino; esso viene come una devastazione dell’Onnipotente. (13:6).
Therefore all hands will be feeble, and every human heart will melt (13:7).
They will be dismayed: pangs and agony will seize them; they will be in anguish like a woman in labor. They will look aghast at one another; their faces will be aflame (13:8).
Behold, the day of il SIGNORE comes, cruel, with wrath and fierce anger, to make the land a desolation and to destroy its sinners from it (13:9).
Poiché le stelle e le costellazioni del cielo non faranno più brillare la loro luce; il sole si oscurerà mentre sorge, la luna non farà più risplendere il suo chiarore. (13:10).
Io punirò il mondo per la sua malvagità e gli empi per la loro iniquità; farò cessare l’alterigia dei superbi e abbatterò l’arroganza dei tiranni. (13:11).
"I will make people more rare than fine gold, and mankind than the gold of Ophir" (13:12).
Perciò farò tremare i cieli, e la terra sarà scossa dal suo luogo per l’indignazione del Signore degli eserciti, nel giorno della sua ira furente. (13:13).
And like a hunted gazelle, or like sheep with none to gather them, each will turn to his own people, and each will flee to his own land (13:14).
Whoever is found will be thrust through, and whoever is caught will fall by the sword (13:15).
Their infants will be dashed in pieces before their eyes; their houses will be plundered and their wives violated (13:16).
"Behold, I am stirring up the Medes against them, who have no regard for silver and do not delight in gold" (13:17).
Their bows will slaughter the young men; they will have no mercy on the fruit of the womb; their eyes will not pity children (13:18).
And Babylon, the glory of kingdoms, the splendor and pomp of the Chaldeans, will be like Sodom and Gomorrah when God overthrew them (13:19).
It will never be inhabited or lived in for all generations; no Arab will pitch his tent there; no shepherds will make their flocks lie down there (13:20).
But wild animals will lie down there, and their houses will be full of howling creatures; there ostriches will dwell, and there wild goats will dance (13:21).
Hyenas will cry in its towers, and jackals in the pleasant palaces; its time is close at hand, and its days will not be prolonged (13:22).

stories.title: 🏛️ Isaia 14
summaryBullets: For il SIGNORE will have compassion on Jacob and will again choose Israel, and will set them in their own land, and sojourners will join them and will attach themselves to the house of Jacob (14:1).

I popoli li prenderanno e li ricondurranno al loro luogo, e la casa d’Israele li possederà nel paese del Signore come servi e come serve; essi terranno prigionieri quelli che li avevano fatti prigionieri e domineranno sui loro oppressori. (14:2).
When il SIGNORE has given you rest from your pain and turmoil and the hard service with which you were made to serve (14:3).
You will take up this taunt against the king of Babylon: "How the oppressor has ceased, the insolent fury ceased!" (14:4).
Il Signore ha spezzato il bastone degli empi, lo scettro dei despoti. (14:5).
That struck the peoples in wrath with unceasing blows, that ruled the nations in anger with unrelenting persecution (14:6).
The whole earth is at rest and quiet; they break forth into singing (14:7).
The cypresses rejoice at you, the cedars of Lebanon, saying, "Since you were laid low, no woodcutter comes up against us" (14:8).

Il soggiorno dei morti, laggiù, si agita per te, per venire a incontrarti al tuo arrivo; esso sveglia per te le ombre, tutti i prìncipi della terra; fa alzare dai loro troni tutti i re delle nazioni. (14:9).
All of them will answer and say to you: "You too have become as weak as we! You have become like us!" (14:10).
Your pomp is brought down to Sheol, the sound of your harps; maggots are laid as a bed beneath you, and worms are your covers (14:11).
Come mai sei caduto dal cielo, astro mattutino, figlio dell’aurora? Come mai sei atterrato, tu che calpestavi le nazioni? (14:12).
Tu dicevi in cuor tuo: “Io salirò in cielo, innalzerò il mio trono al di sopra delle stelle di Dio; mi siederò sul monte dell’assemblea, nella parte estrema del settentrione; (14:13).
"I will ascend above the heights of the clouds; I will make myself like the Most High" (14:14).
Invece ti hanno fatto discendere nel soggiorno dei morti, nelle profondità della fossa! (14:15).
Those who see you will stare at you and ponder over you: "Is this the man who made the earth tremble, who shook kingdoms" (14:16).
"Who made the world like a desert and overthrew its cities, who did not let his prisoners go home?" (14:17).
All the kings of the nations lie in glory, each in his own tomb (14:18).
ma tu sei stato gettato lontano dalla tua tomba come un rampollo abominevole coperto di uccisi trafitti con la spada, calati sotto i sassi della fossa, come un cadavere calpestato. (14:19).
You will not be joined with them in burial, because you have destroyed your land, you have slain your people. May the offspring of evildoers nevermore be named! (14:20).
Preparate il massacro dei suoi figli, a causa dell’iniquità dei loro padri! Che non si rialzino più a conquistare la terra, a riempire il mondo di città! (14:21).
"I will rise up against them," declares il SIGNORE of hosts, "and will cut off from Babylon name and remnant, descendants and posterity," declares il SIGNORE (14:22).
"And I will make it a possession of the hedgehog, and pools of water, and I will sweep it with the broom of destruction," declares il SIGNORE of hosts (14:23).
The LORD of hosts has sworn: "As I have planned, so shall it be, and as I have purposed, so shall it stand" (14:24).
"That I will break the Assyrian in My land, and on My mountains trample him underfoot; and his yoke shall depart from them, and his burden from their shoulder" (14:25).
This is the purpose that is purposed concerning the whole earth, and this is the hand that is stretched out over all the nations (14:26).
For il SIGNORE of hosts has purposed, and who will annul it? His hand is stretched out, and who will turn it back? (14:27).
In the year that King Ahaz died came this oracle (14:28).
"Rejoice not, O Philistia, all of you, that the rod that struck you is broken, for from the serpent's root will come forth an adder, and its fruit will be a flying fiery serpent" (14:29).
I più poveri avranno di che pascersi e i bisognosi riposeranno al sicuro; ma io farò morire di fame la tua radice e quel che rimarrà di te sarà ucciso. (14:30).
Wail, O gate; cry out, O city; melt in fear, O Philistia, all of you! For smoke comes out of the north, and there is no straggler in his ranks (14:31).
Che cosa si risponderà ai messaggeri di questa nazione? «Che il Signore ha fondato Sion e che in essa gli afflitti del suo popolo trovano rifugio». (14:32).

stories.title: 🏜️ Isaia 15
summaryBullets: An oracle concerning Moab. Because Ar of Moab is laid waste in a night, Moab is undone; because Kir of Moab is laid waste in a night, Moab is undone (15:1).
Si sale al tempio e a Dibon, sugli alti luoghi, per piangere; Moab urla su Nebo e su Medeba: tutte le teste sono rase, tutte le barbe sono tagliate. (15:2).
Per le strade tutti indossano sacchi, sui tetti e per le piazze ognuno urla, piangendo a dirotto. (15:3).
Heshbon and Elealeh cry out; their voice is heard as far as Jahaz; therefore the armed men of Moab cry aloud; his soul trembles (15:4).
My heart cries out for Moab; her fugitives flee to Zoar, to Eglath-shelishiyah. For at the ascent of Luhith they go up weeping; on the road to Horonaim they raise a cry of destruction (15:5).
For the waters of Nimrim are a desolation; the grass is withered, the vegetation fails, the greenery is no more (15:6).
Therefore the abundance they have gained and what they have laid up they carry away over the Brook of the Willows (15:7).
For a cry has gone around the land of Moab; her wailing reaches to Eglaim; her wailing reaches to Beer-elim (15:8).
Le acque di Dimon sono piene di sangue, ma infliggerò a Dimon nuovi guai: un leone contro gli scampati di Moab e contro quel che resta del paese. (15:9).

stories.title: 🏜️ Isaia 16
summaryBullets: Mandate gli agnelli per il dominatore del paese, mandateli da Sela, per la via del deserto, al monte della figlia di Sion! (16:1).
Like fleeing birds, like a scattered nest, so are the daughters of Moab at the fords of the Arnon (16:2).
"Give counsel; grant justice; make your shade like night at the height of noon; shelter the outcasts; do not reveal the fugitive" (16:3).

lascia abitare presso di te gli esuli di Moab, sii tu per loro un rifugio contro il devastatore! L’oppressione infatti è finita, la devastazione è cessata, gli invasori sono scomparsi dal paese. (16:4).
Then a throne will be established in steadfast love, and on it will sit in faithfulness in the tent of David one who judges and seeks justice and is swift to do righteousness (16:5).
We have heard of the pride of Moab—how proud he is!—of his arrogance, his pride, and his insolence; in his idle boasting he is not right (16:6).
Therefore let Moab wail; let everyone wail for Moab. Mourn, utterly stricken, for the raisin cakes of Kir-hareseth (16:7).

stories.title: 🌪️ Isaia 17
summaryBullets: An oracle concerning Damascus. Behold, Damascus will cease to be a city and will become a heap of ruins (17:1).
The cities of Aroer are deserted; they will be for flocks, which will lie down, and none will make them afraid (17:2).
Non ci sarà più fortezza in Efraim né reame in Damasco; del residuo di Siria avverrà ciò che è avvenuto della gloria dei figli d’Israele», dice il Signore degli eserciti. (17:3).
And in that day the glory of Jacob will be brought low, and the fat of his flesh will grow lean (17:4).
Avverrà come quando il mietitore raccoglie il grano e con il braccio falcia le spighe; avverrà come quando si raccolgono le spighe nella valle di Refaim. (17:5).
Vi rimarrà qualcosa da spigolare, come quando si scuote l’olivo: restano due o tre olive nelle cime più alte, quattro o cinque nei rami più carichi», dice il Signore, Dio d’Israele. (17:6).
In that day man will look to his Maker, and his eyes will look on the Holy One of Israel (17:7).
He will not look to the altars, the work of his hands, and he will not look on what his own fingers have made, either the Asherim or the altars of incense (17:8).
In quel giorno le sue fortezze saranno abbandonate, come le foreste e le sommità dei monti furono abbandonate all’avvicinarsi dei figli d’Israele: sarà una desolazione. (17:9).
For you have forgotten the God of your salvation and have not remembered the Rock of your refuge; therefore, though you plant pleasant plants and sow the vine-branch of a stranger (17:10).
Though you make them grow on the day that you plant them, and make them blossom in the morning that you sow, yet the harvest will flee away in a day of grief and incurable pain (17:11).
Ah, the thunder of many peoples; they thunder like the thundering of the sea! Ah, the roar of nations; they roar like the roaring of mighty waters! (17:12).
The nations roar like the roaring of many waters, but He will rebuke them, and they will flee far away, chased like chaff on the mountains before the wind and whirling dust before the storm (17:13).
At evening time, behold, terror! Before morning, they are no more! This is the portion of those who plunder us, and the lot of those who despoil us (17:14).

stories.title: 🛶 Isaia 18
summaryBullets: Ah, land of whirring wings that is beyond the rivers of Cush (18:1).

Which sends ambassadors by the sea, in vessels of papyrus on the waters! Go, you swift messengers, to a nation tall and smooth, to a people feared near and far, a nation mighty and conquering, whose land the rivers divide (18:2).
All you inhabitants of the world, you who dwell on the earth, when a signal is raised on the mountains, look! When a trumpet is blown, hear! (18:3).
Poiché così mi ha detto il Signore: «Io me ne starò tranquillo e guarderò dal mio posto, come un calore sereno alla luce del sole, come una nube di rugiada nel calore della mietitura». (18:4).
For before the harvest, when the blossom is over, and the flower becomes a ripening grape, He cuts off the shoots with pruning hooks and removes and cuts away the spreading branches (18:5).

Gli Assiri saranno tutti assieme abbandonati agli uccelli rapaci dei monti e alle bestie della terra: gli uccelli rapaci passeranno l’estate sui loro cadaveri e le bestie della terra vi passeranno l’inverno. (18:6).

At that time tribute will be brought to il SIGNORE of hosts from a people tall and smooth, from a people feared near and far, a nation mighty and conquering, whose land the rivers divide, to Mount Zion, the place of the name of il SIGNORE of hosts (18:7).

stories.title: ☁️ Isaia 19
summaryBullets: Oracolo sull’Egitto. Ecco, il Signore cavalca una nuvola leggera ed entra in Egitto; gli idoli d’Egitto tremano davanti a lui e all’Egitto si scioglie il cuore nel petto. (19:1).
"And I will stir up Egyptians against Egyptians, and they will fight, each against another and each against his neighbor, city against city, kingdom against kingdom" (19:2).
Lo spirito che anima l’Egitto svanirà, io renderò vani i suoi disegni; quelli consulteranno gli idoli, gli incantatori, gli evocatori di spiriti e gli indovini. (19:3).
"And I will give over the Egyptians into the hand of a hard master, and a fierce king will rule over them," declares the Lord GOD of hosts (19:4).
Le acque verranno meno al mare, il fiume diverrà secco, arido; (19:5).
And its canals will become foul, and the branches of Egypt's Nile will diminish and dry up, and reeds and rushes will rot away (19:6).
There will be bare places by the Nile, on the brink of the Nile, and all that is sown by the Nile will be parched, will be driven away, and will be no more (19:7).
The fishermen will mourn and lament, all who cast a hook in the Nile; and they who spread nets on the water will languish (19:8).
The workers in combed flax will be in despair, and the weavers of white cotton (19:9).
Those who are the pillars of the land will be crushed, and all who work for pay will be grieved (19:10).

I prìncipi di Soan non sono che degli stolti; i più saggi tra i consiglieri del faraone danno dei consigli insensati. Come potete mai dire al faraone: «Io sono figlio dei saggi, figlio degli antichi re?» (19:11).
Where then are your wise men? Let them tell you that they might know what il SIGNORE of hosts has purposed against Egypt (19:12).
The princes of Zoan have become fools, and the princes of Memphis are deluded; those who are the cornerstones of her tribes have led Egypt astray (19:13).
The LORD has mingled within her a spirit of confusion, and they will make Egypt stagger in all its deeds, as a drunken man staggers in his vomit (19:14).
And there will be nothing for Egypt that head or tail, palm branch or reed, may do (19:15).
In that day the Egyptians will be like women, and tremble with fear before the hand that il SIGNORE of hosts shakes over them (19:16).
Il paese di Giuda sarà il terrore dell’Egitto; tutte le volte che gli verrà menzionato, ne sarà spaventato a causa della decisione presa contro di lui dal Signore degli eserciti. (19:17).
In that day there will be five cities in il paese d’Egitto that speak the language of Canaan and swear allegiance to il SIGNORE of hosts. One of these will be called the City of Destruction (19:18).
In that day there will be an altar to il SIGNORE in the midst of il paese d’Egitto, and a pillar to il SIGNORE at its border (19:19).
It will be a sign and a witness to il SIGNORE of hosts in il paese d’Egitto. When they cry to il SIGNORE because of oppressors, He will send them a savior and defender, and deliver them (19:20).
Il Signore si farà conoscere all’Egitto e gli Egiziani, in quel giorno, conosceranno il Signore, gli offriranno un culto con sacrifici e offerte, faranno voti al Signore e li adempiranno. (19:21).
The LORD will strike Egypt, striking and healing, and they will return to il SIGNORE, and He will listen to their pleas for mercy and heal them (19:22).
In that day there will be a highway from Egypt to Assyria, and Assyria will come into Egypt, and Egypt into Assyria, and the Egyptians will worship with the Assyrians (19:23).
In quel giorno Israele sarà terzo con l’Egitto e con l’Assiria, e tutti e tre saranno una benedizione in mezzo alla terra. (19:24).
Whom il SIGNORE of hosts has blessed, saying, "Blessed be Egypt My people, and Assyria the work of My hands, and Israel My inheritance" (19:25).

così il re d’Assiria condurrà via i prigionieri dall’Egitto e i deportati dall’Etiopia, giovani e vecchi, seminudi e scalzi, con le natiche scoperte, a vergogna dell’Egitto. (20:4).

stories.title: 🕯️ Isaia 21
summaryBullets: Oracolo contro il deserto marittimo. Come gli uragani, quando si scatenano, nella regione meridionale, egli viene dal deserto, da un paese spaventoso. (21:1).
A stern vision is told to me: the traitor betrays, and the destroyer destroys. "Go up, O Elam; lay siege, O Media; all the sighing she has caused I bring to an end" (21:2).
Therefore my loins are filled with anguish; pangs have seized me, like the pangs of a woman in labor; I am bowed down so that I cannot hear; I am dismayed so that I cannot see (21:3).
My heart staggers; horror has appalled me; the twilight I longed for has been turned for me into trembling (21:4).
They prepare the table, they spread the rugs, they eat, they drink. "Arise, O princes; oil the shield!" (21:5).
Poiché così mi ha parlato il Signore: «Va’, metti una sentinella; che essa annunci quanto vedrà! (21:6).
"When he sees riders, horsemen in pairs, riders on donkeys, riders on camels, let him listen diligently, very diligently" (21:7).
Then he who saw cried out: "Upon a watchtower I stand, O Lord, continually by day, and at my post I am stationed whole nights" (21:8).
Ed ecco venire un carro con un uomo e due cavalli. Quello gridava: “Caduta, caduta è Babilonia! E tutte le immagini scolpite dei suoi dèi sono frantumate al suolo”». (21:9).
O my threshed and winnowed one, what I have heard from il SIGNORE of hosts, the God of Israel, I announce to you (21:10).
Oracolo contro Duma. Mi si grida da Seir: «Sentinella, a che punto è la notte? Sentinella, a che punto è la notte?» (21:11).
The watchman says, "Morning comes, and also the night. If you will inquire, inquire; come back again" (21:12).
The oracle concerning Arabia. In the thickets in Arabia you will lodge, O caravans of Dedanites (21:13).
Venite incontro all’assetato con acqua, o abitanti del paese di Tema; portate pane ai fuggiaschi. (21:14).
Poiché essi fuggono davanti alle spade, davanti alla spada sguainata, davanti all’arco teso, davanti al furore della battaglia. (21:15).
Poiché così mi ha parlato il Signore: «Fra un anno, contato come quello di un operaio, tutta la gloria di Chedar sarà svanita; (21:16).
ciò che resterà del numero dei valorosi arcieri di Chedar sarà poca cosa»; poiché il Signore, Dio d’Israele, l’ha detto. (21:17).
